# onetsolutions_hosting_subdomain (Resource)

Manages a subdomain of the main domain of a web hosting.

The web hosting must be active. A subdomain cannot be changed in place: changing `subdomain` or
`document_root` removes it and adds the new one. Terraform refuses to add a subdomain the web
hosting already has; import it instead, by its full domain name or by its label alone. The site
is reachable once the name resolves to the web hosting.

If the subdomain is removed outside Terraform, the next plan adds it again. Once the web hosting
is cancelled or terminated, the next refresh removes the subdomain from the state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_web_hosting" "site" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

resource "onetsolutions_hosting_subdomain" "blog" {
  hosting_id    = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  subdomain     = "blog"
  document_root = "public_html/blog"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `hosting_id` (String) The UUID of the web hosting the subdomain belongs to. Changing it recreates the subdomain.
- `subdomain` (String) The subdomain, without the main domain: `blog` for `blog.example.com`. Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and dots, 63 characters at most. Changing it recreates the subdomain.

### Optional

- `document_root` (String) The directory the subdomain serves, relative to the account's home directory, such as `public_html/blog`. When unset, the web hosting's default directory for the subdomain. The web hosting does not report it, so a change made outside Terraform is not detected, and after an import the configured value is taken as it is. Changing it recreates the subdomain.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.

### Read-Only

- `domain` (String) The main domain of the web hosting.
- `id` (String) The full domain name of the subdomain, such as `blog.example.com`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_hosting_subdomain.blog
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/blog.example.com"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<hosting_id>/<subdomain>, or <hosting_id>/<subdomain> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
terraform import onetsolutions_hosting_subdomain.blog 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/blog.example.com
```
